Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 31788 of 2023

Applicant :- Hussain
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Sayeed Saif Ullah,Sufia Saba
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Ms. Sufia Saba, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ravi Kant Kushwaha, learned
Aga for the State-respondent.

2.  The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
197 of 2023, under Sections 376, 506 IPC, Police Station- Khatauli, District- Muzaffar Nagar, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

entities.text: Police Station- Khatauli, District- Muzaffar Nagar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
3. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant on 25.04.2023 under Sections 376, 506 IPC and according to the FIR, applicant about three years before committed rape with the informant i.e. prosecutrix of the case and also prepared her indecent videographs and on 04.04.2023, he again committed rape with her and thereafter in the 'Panchayat' it was settled that applicant will perform marriage with her but subsequently he refused to perform marriage with the informant i.e.
prosecutrix of the case.

Hussain vs State Of U.P. on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79176546/
1 4.

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegation of rape and sexual exploitation made against the applicant in the FIR as well as in the statements of the victim recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. is totally false and baseless and actually victim and applicant were in love and they performed marriage according to Muslim rites and rituals on 05.04.2023 but after that some dispute arose between both the sides and thereafter on 25.04.2023 i.e. after about 20 days from the date of marriage of the applicant and victim, FIR of the present case was lodged on the basis of false and frivolous allegation.
She further submitted that 'Nikahnama' of the applicant and the informant has been annexed as Annexure No. 6 to the affidavit.

5. She further submitted that even from the FIR and the statements of the victim recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C., it appears that victim was a major girl and she was consenting party and in spite of allegation that applicant prepared indecent videographs of the victim, no such videographs could be recovered during investigation.

6. She further submitted that in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. victim added two more accused persons and stated that applicant and two others committed rape with her and this fact suggests that prosecutrix of the case is not a reliable witness.
He further submitted that applicant is not having any criminal history and he is in jail since 10.06.2023.

7. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that there is allegation of rape and sexual exploitation against the applicant in the FIR as well as in both the statements of the victim recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. but could not dispute the fact that victim is a major girl and she appears to be consenting party and during investigation no alleged indecent videographs of the victim could be recovered and even in his instruction the genuineness of the 'Nikahnama' could not be controverted.
8.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

9. Although, in the FIR as well as in both the statements of the victim recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C., there is allegation of rape and sexual exploitation against the applicant but it reflects that victim is a major girl and according to Annexure No. 6, victim and applicant had already performed marriage according to Muslim rites and rituals and fact of marriage has not been specifically denied by learned AGA.
10. Further, although, there is allegation of preparation of indecent videographs of the victim against the applicant but during investigation, no such videographs could be recovered.
11. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
12. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

Hussain vs State Of U.P. on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79176546/
2 13.

Let the applicant- Hussain be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
14. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

15. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
Order Date :- 20.7.2023
KK Patel
